sentences.text: Gregory S. Paul estimated that this predator reached a total length of 4.5 meters and a mass of 200 kilograms.
The holotype ilium, which is the pelvic bone used to define the species, measures 37.5 centimeters in length.
If the available cranial fragments belong to Marshosaurus, the skull would have been approximately 60 centimeters long.
James Henry Madsen Jr. formally named the type species Marshosaurus bicentesimus in 1976.
The genus name honors the famous paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh.
The specific name bicentesimus was selected to celebrate the bicentennial of the United States of America.
The holotype specimen was discovered in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation, dating to approximately 155 to 152 million years ago.
Current fossil material represents at least three distinct individuals of this dinosaur.
One right ilium of Marshosaurus bicentesimus displays deformation that likely resulted from a physical injury.
This specific pelvic bone shows signs of pathology, confirming that the animal suffered from a health issue during its life.
A separate Marshosaurus specimen possesses a pathological rib, indicating further evidence of disease or trauma.
A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild found no signs of stress fractures in five foot bones referred to Marshosaurus.
Research by Bruce Rothschild and others examined five foot bones for stress fractures but found none.
Roger Benson classified Marshosaurus as a megalosauroid in a 2010 phylogenetic analysis.
Marshosaurus is currently classified as a member of the family Piatnitzkysauridae.
The animal belongs to the class Reptilia.
Marshosaurus lived in the Late Jurassic Morrison Formation of Utah and possibly Colorado.
This dinosaur lived between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages.
The environment of the Morrison Formation is interpreted as semiarid with distinct wet and dry seasons.
The Morrison Formation environment was interpreted as a semi-arid environment with distinct wet and dry seasons.
The Morrison Formation environment was dominated by giant sauropod dinosaurs such as Camarasaurus, Brachiosaurus, Barosaurus, Diplodocus, and Apatosaurus.
Marshosaurus lived alongside ornithischian herbivores including Camptosaurus, Dryosaurus, Stegosaurus, and Othnielosaurus.
Predators in the Marshosaurus paleoenvironment included theropods such as Saurophaganax, Torvosaurus, Ceratosaurus, Stokesosaurus, Ornitholestes, and Allosaurus.
Early mammals, including docodonts, multituberculates, symmetrodonts, and triconodonts, were present in the region.
The flora of the time included green algae, fungi, mosses, horsetails, cycads, ginkgos, and various conifer families.
Vegetation in the area ranged from riverbank forests of ferns and tree ferns to fern savannas with occasional trees like the araucaria Brachyphyllum.
